content_sections.body: In service request, put finished actions in a clear order. Use time words such as yesterday, first, then, and this morning. Example: “My card did not work at the machine, so I asked a staff member for help..” The past action tells the listener what happened; the time word tells when.
content_sections.title: Notice the language

content_sections.body: My card did not work at the machine, so I asked a staff member for help. Ask: what detail would a friend need next? Say the key action once, then add one time or place detail.
content_sections.title: Context and meaning

content_sections.body: Choose a true or invented service request detail. Say two connected sentences: one about what happened and one about the next step. Check that the order is easy to follow.

listening.goal: Catch the main event and one detail about service request.
listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about service request. Answer one question before seeing the transcript. Then listen again and notice the sequence words.

pronunciation.goal: Make the event order and main action easy to hear.
pronunciation.instruction: Practise the concrete sound target for service request: group the message into two thought groups and stress the main action word. Read the example slowly, then at natural speed.

constraints: Use at most three tutor turns.
Stop after agreeing on a next step.
speaking.goal: Complete a useful exchange about service request.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a customer or friend dealing with service request; the tutor is the staff member or friend who has one missing detail. Scenario: explain what happened and ask for the next step. Tutor opening: “Hi, what happened?” Ask one follow-up about time, place, quantity, or result; finish when the tutor understands and you agree on the next step.

constraints: Do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a clear short message about service request.
writing.instruction: Write 3 short sentences about service request: say what happened, add when or where, and say what happened next. Submit your draft first.
